results.reason: Issue 1 quotes Supply Agreement §14.2: a change of more than 50% ownership is deemed an assignment requiring Supplier's prior written consent, with a 30-day termination right. It notes Schedule 4.4 says 'None' and that the §7.2(c) condition is therefore automatically satisfied.
The response never discusses Supply Agreement §16.1. It does not raise Vantrell's unilateral assignment right or the risk that the contract passes to a competitor.
Issue 2 counts back 120 days from Dec 31, 2026 to about Sept 2, 2026. It notes the SPA was dated Sept 21, 2026, so the option has lapsed and the Extension Pricing is lost.
Issue 3 states the Side Letter §2 redefinition controls under §11.11. It explains that 4.3 and 4.12 become subject to the deductible and the 10% cap.

Issue 4 identifies Side Letter §6.1/6.2 (Delaware law, Chancery) conflicting with SPA §11.8/11.9 (New York), which splits law and forum. The precedence clause is not repeated in this section, but §11.11's Side Letter priority is established in Issue 3 and treated as controlling.
The response repeatedly references the '10% cap' alongside the $84.5M Purchase Price.
The response states 'SPA, Section 11.11 (Order of Precedence: Side Letter first)'.
The memo is addressed to [Partner]. Each issue gives the documents and sections, why it matters to Halvorsen, and a recommendation.
Issues are ordered critical first (supply consent, lapsed option) and the low-priority item comes later. The memo includes a dedicated table of items requiring a client call.
The response states the option has lapsed.
The response states that Capitalization and Taxes are demoted and capped, and that the Side Letter controls.
